transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 65m | Attendees: Sam Patel, Lina Gomez, Priya Rao (Redwood); Michael Lee, Jasmine Carter, David Wong, Erin Park (Aurora)

Summary: Quick follow-up to last week's outage affecting inference throughput for aurora-prod, review of RCA, mitigations we applied, and next steps for reliability improvements and runbook drills.

[00:00] Sam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run through the timeline then Lina will go over the fix and tests, and Priya will outline operational follow-ups. Michael, can you open with any missed context?
[00:15] Michael: Yeah thanks. Uh so the outage on 7/30 impacted our customer-facing recommendations service - latency spiked and some requests 504ed. We already reopened tickets with our incident channel but want to align on RCA and what permanent mitigations look like.
[01:05] Sam: Absolutely. Quick note - transcription may be a little rough on some product names. We called out KV cache and autoscaler, so apologies if things sound off.
[02:10] Lina: I'll walk through the timeline we collected. At ~14:03 UTC we saw an increase in request fan-out from our batcher; autoscaler attempted to spin up extra workers but hit a provisioning limit for the dedicated pool. Meanwhile prefix/KV cache misses increased because a rollout yesterday changed tokenization which invalidated some prefixes. The combination increased per-request compute and queue depth.
[03:00] Jasmine: Right and just to add, our logs show cache hit-rate dropped from ~85% to ~44% across the window. Key-value cache TTLs were shorter than expected after the deploy.
[03:40] Sam: So two main vectors: cache invalidation from model/rollout change and capacity exhaustion because the dedicated pool couldn't burst quickly enough. Any contention on that?
[04:05] David: From a security/compliance lens we saw several retries that triggered rate limits in front of the SSO tokens - some requests ended up reauthing which added latency. We want to make sure these retry paths are logged for audits.
[05:00] Priya: On our side we triggered the fallback to hosted model variant as intended but the routing config had a short cooldown, so we didn't failover fast enough. That's partly why we saw user-facing errors even with a fallback policy.
[06:30] Lina: The immediate mitigation we pushed was twofold: 1) revert the tokenization change in the rollout which restored prefix mapping, 2) increase provisional burst capacity for Aurora's dedicated pool and raise autoscaler upper bound. That reduced queue depth and latency within ~20 minutes.
[07:10] Michael: That aligns with what we saw. The revert helped, but we needed the reprovision to avoid a second spike.
[08:00] Lina: We also applied a hotfix to the batcher to reduce aggressive fan-out for large prompts which prevented amplified concurrency from a single request. Tests show that reduces peak concurrent requests by ~30%.
[09:00] Erin: Quick question - is the fan-out change persistent or a temporary throttle? We want to understand any impact on quality.
[09:25] Lina: It's a conservative throttle in the batcher; we ran internal quality tests across our eval set and saw negligible degradation for recommendation prompts. That said, it's toggled as a config flag so we can revert if you see regressions.
[10:45] Jasmine: In terms of observability gaps, we had delayed tracing for the KV cache invalidation. End-to-end traces weren't retained beyond 24h due to retention settings, so correlating requests to cache misses took longer.
[12:00] Priya: Action items: Redwood will produce a full RCA doc with exact timeline, evidence, and mitigation steps. We'll also propose an updated failover policy: shorter routing cooldown + staged canary validation for tokenization-related deploys.
[13:20] Michael: On the Aurora side we need better pre-deploy smoke tests that check cache hit-rate and tokenization compatibility across our prompts. We'll share a subset of canary prompt sets.
[14:00] Lina: Technical deep dive - root cause in detail: the tokenization change altered the prefix boundary which meant the cache key calculation produced different keys for many frequent prefixes. Combined with an incomplete cache warm-up during rolling deploy, this caused a big cold-start effect. The autoscaler also had a hard limit set in reserved capacity which we've adjusted.
[15:40] Sam: We should also document the twist where the routing fallback had a cooldown tied to origin model version, which didn't trigger because the canary passed a superficial health check. So the system estimated healthy and didn't fallback. We'll propose a secondary health metric tied to latency and error rate.
[17:00] David: For compliance, can you confirm the audit logs include the fallback events, routing decisions, and tokenization version? We need those persisted in the retention window for SOC2 audits.
[17:25] Priya: Yes, we will capture routing decisions and model version in audit logs. We'll extend retention for Aurora to 90 days as an add-on and provide exports on request.
[19:00] Michael: Regarding the dedicated pool provisioning limit - why didn't autoscaler spin beyond the cap? Is that a soft limit we can bump?
[19:30] Lina: It was a configured cap tied to your committed capacity. We can temporarily increase burst capacity during the deploy window, and we recommend a scheduled buffer for critical rollout windows. We'll send recommended thresholds and cost tradeoffs.
[21:10] Erin: On the security thread, David noted token reauths. Can we get more structured logs around retry counts per token and whether tokens were expired vs throttled?
[21:40] David: Also, please indicate whether those retries are client's retry logic or our internal retry; for audits we need to distinguish.
[22:20] Lina: We'll add fields to request logs to indicate origin of retry and auth response codes. That will help correlate.
[24:00] Sam: Let's talk about the runbook and triage flow changes: we propose a 3-stage runbook - A) immediate mitigation steps (revert rollout, increase burst), B) diagnostic steps (collect cache metrics, trace samples), C) recovery and communication (customer status page updates). We'll share a template.
[26:10] Jasmine: One of our delays was getting the right trace slice to analyze KV cache. If Redwood can provide a pre-built dashboard showing cache hit-rate, TTL, and per-model prefix distribution, that will speed future RCA.
[27:00] Priya: We'll build a dashboard and add a per-customer prescriptive alert when hit-rate drops by >20% in 5 minutes. We'll also surface a warm-up checklist for deploys that touch tokenization or tokenizer models.
[29:00] Lina: On the reliability improvements list: 1) stricter canary checks that include cache key stability, 2) autoscaler delta policies that allow temporary burst above committed capacity when explicit flag is set, 3) improved retention for traces and audit logs for enterprise customers.
[31:00] Michael: Sounds good. What about longer-term options? We discussed dedicated private deployment - would moving to Private (VPC) remove this class of issue?
[31:35] Sam: Private deployments reduce network variability and give you direct control over autoscaler config, but they don't change model tokenization mismatch risk. They help with latency and isolation but you'd still need canary checks and cache warm-up in any environment.
[33:00] Erin: Any mitigation we should do immediately before the next deploy?
[33:20] Lina: Yes - require tokenization compatibility smoke tests in CI (we'll help define), set a canary traffic window of at least 5-10% for 30 minutes, and provision a temporary burst buffer for the rollout. Also increase KV cache TTLs during the rollout to reduce cold-start effect.
[35:00] Michael: On cost tradeoffs - bumping burst capacity will increase spend. Can you provide cost delta scenarios (small/medium/large) for the proposed buffers?
[35:30] Sam: We'll provide a short spreadsheet with cost estimates and expected latency improvement per tier.
[36:45] David: Another compliance ask: we need a written note that rollback preserves audit trail and that model versions are immutable in logs.
[37:00] Priya: We'll include that in the RCA and the runbook; model versions logged and immutable, rollbacks generate an event with who/when/reason.
[38:50] Jasmine: Regarding testing - can Redwood run a scheduled load test on a staging copy of Aurora's traffic pattern? We want to validate the fan-out patch and autoscaler changes.
[39:20] Lina: Yes, we can run targeted benchmark tests. We'll need a traffic sample and a window to run. We'll include tests for KV cache hit-rate, latency tail percentiles, and provisioning time for the dedicated pool.
[41:00] Sam: Let's capture decisions: revert tokenization change (done), broaden autoscaler caps and burst (in progress), apply batcher fan-out throttle (done), add extra observability dashboards and traces (planned), extend audit log retention for Aurora (planned).
[42:30] Erin: For the canary policy, can we have Redwood run a canary on our behalf for the next two deploys and shadow traffic to catch cache key regressions?
[43:00] Priya: Yes, we can run managed canaries for two deploys as part of the support engagement. We'll define the criteria upfront.
[44:30] Michael: Anything on RBAC or SSO we need to tweak? We want a tighter control so retries don't trigger sensitive throttles.
[45:00] David: Also need to ensure token refresh logic is logged at the SSO layer; sometimes refreshes look like new sessions which confuses audit trails.
[45:40] Lina: We'll coordinate with your security team to ensure token refreshes and retry attribution are surfaced in logs separately.
[47:00] Sam: Cost/packaging note: for the extended retention & managed canary we'll propose a short-term support add-on and revised committed capacity for one quarter. Pricing and options will be in the follow-up email.
[48:10] Michael: Ok good. Quick check - does Redwood have an automated warm-up path for KV cache after deploys? We heard about prefix warm-up but not a full solution.
[48:40] Lina: We have a warm-up API that can be used to prepopulate cache with a curated prompt set; we'll provide a script that runs as part of your CI pipeline. We'll also document recommended TTL settings.
[50:00] Erin: When can we expect the final RCA and the runbook?
[50:10] Sam: We'll deliver RCA by 2026-08-06 and share the runbook and dashboard drafts by 2026-08-10.
[51:00] Jasmine: For the audit logs extension, how do we handle exports for auditors? Flat files or API access?
[51:30] Priya: We'll provide both: API access to the retained logs plus an export package on request. We'll coordinate S3 export permissions.
[53:00] Michael: Any blockers from Redwood to implementing the temporary burst during next deploy?
[53:20] Lina: No blockers; we just need confirmation on the window and the desired buffer size. We'll also share cost estimates for three buffer tiers.
[55:00] Sam: Let's recap and confirm action owners. (Sam reads action items).
[56:30] Erin: We'll schedule an internal Aurora pre-deploy smoke for tokenization compatibility and share prompt sets by 2026-08-05.
[57:10] Michael: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the quick response from Redwood.
[58:00] Sam: Thanks - we'll follow up with the RCA and the cost spreadsheet. If no more questions we'll end early.
[58:25] David: One last compliance Q - can you add a short writeup on how rollback events are correlated with audit logs? We need to present that to audit next week.
[58:40] Priya: Yes, we'll include a rollback-audit appendix in the RCA doc.
[59:00] Sam: Great, thanks all. End call.
